claim: In a seismic-facies semantic segmentation task, a 30-member deep ensemble's predictive-entropy uncertainty correlates with actual per-pixel prediction error at Pearson r=0.715 (+/-0.081) and Spearman rho=0.568 (+/-0.108).
stance_target: the audited paper's claim that ensemble sigma correlates with error at only rho~=0.07
scope_conditions: dense per-pixel classification (semantic segmentation) of seismic facies volumes, M=30 ensemble members, apparently in-distribution test data
quoted_support: Deep Ensemble [10]        0.715 ± 0.081 0.568 ± 0.108 0.661 ± 0.114 [Table 2, Agreement with Prediction Error]

claim: This result is domain-mismatched relative to the audited paper (dense per-pixel classification/segmentation, not scalar regression) and comes from a very recent (2026), not-yet-heavily-cited conference paper, warranting lower evidentiary weight than a peer-reviewed regression benchmark.
stance_target: evidentiary strength/generalizability of the RADMI correlation figures
scope_conditions: IEEE ICIP 2026 accepted paper, seismic imaging domain
quoted_support: Citation W. Stevens, M. Prabhushankar, and G. AlRegib, "RADMI: Latent Information Aggregation as a Proxy for Model Uncertainty," in IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP), Tampere, Finland, 2026. Review Date of Acceptance: April 30th 2026
